transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-11 11:00 AM PDT | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Samir (Aurelia Head of ML), Maya (Eng Manager), Tom (Security)

Summary: quick run to sign off success criteria and acceptance tests for the 6-week POC. Focus: workload sizing, benchmark plan, go/no-go thresholds, and reporting format. Lots of talk about latency vs cost and private VPC requirements.

Topics: success criteria; benchmark workload (sample sizes, token distributions); run cadence; acceptance report format; security checklist (SOC2, KMS, SAML/SSO); timeline / owners.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Lena: all right everyone thanks for joining, um we're here to lock down the success criteria for the POC, I think we have about 55 minutes, quick intros?
00:12 Samir: hey Samir here, head of ML at Aurelia, we own the model infra and evaluation, excited to get this moving
00:17 Maya: Maya, eng manager, we'll be integrating the inference APIs into our feature service
00:21 Tom: Tom from security, I'll focus on compliance and network constraints
00:26 Marcus: Marcus, se from Redwood, I will run the benchmarks and help with the KV/cache tuning
00:32 Lena: cool, agenda: confirm workload, agree on acceptance tests (go/no-go), decide reporting format and cadence, and next steps

03:05 Maya: quick context - our current traffic pattern is bursty, roughly 15 reqs/s peak, avg payload 350 tokens in, 120 tokens out, 3-4 second client wait tolerable but we want backend p95 low.
03:20 Samir: right, also quality is critical - we need at least 90% acceptable responses on our rubric or we fail the POC, we can detail that rubric later

06:40 Marcus: for sizing we'll run two benchmark buckets - representative (prodsim) of 2k queries and stress of 10k queries to measure throughput and tail latency. We'll warm KV cache with a 1k prefix pass.
06:55 Lena: want to document the acceptance thresholds now? propose: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms for hosted path; for dedicated/pinned capacity p95 < 300ms; availability 99.9% during run; and quality pass rate >= 92% on sampled responses. Thoughts?
07:20 Samir: those numbers look reasonable, question on tokens cost - we need to keep token unit cost under $0.0006 per token average across runs or it'll fail our cost objective
07:35 Tom: security: we need audit logs and KMS integration for keys; for private deployment we need VPC peering + SAML SSO, SOC2 report, and IP allowlist. Can you confirm Redwood can provide those?
07:55 Marcus: yes we can provide SOC2, KMS integration (customer-managed keys in Private), SAML SSO and RBAC. For hosted we provide audit logs via console exports and can push logs to your SIEM.

11:10 Maya: how will you measure quality? automated metrics or human review?
11:20 Marcus: mix - we'll run automatic checks (BLEU/ROUGE-ish heuristics are noisy), but main acceptance is human-rated sample: 200 responses sampled across prompts, rated by Aurelia's rubric with pass/fail. Threshold: >= 92% pass. We'll document the rubric in the acceptance test template.

14:02 Lena: ok acceptance test summary - functional: correctness pass rate >=92% on human sample; performance: p95 latency target as discussed; reliability: no more than 1% errors; cost: avg token cost under $0.0006. If any single threshold is missed it's a potential fail but we agreed to a soft rollback window?
14:22 Samir: yes we want a go/no-go matrix: major items are quality and p95. If quality <85% auto fail; between 85-92% is conditional with remediation window of 1 week to tune prompts/quantization.

18:00 Marcus: about the workload sample - please provide 2 seeds: 1) 2k representative prod-like queries (we'll sample variety of lengths), 2) 10k stress queries. Provide expected reply examples for 500 of the rep queries if you have them. Also indicate any disallowed content so model safety checks can be applied.

21:30 Maya: timeline - we have 6 weeks for POC. Week 1: onboarding + data handoff; Week 2: baseline runs and initial tuning; Weeks 3-4: benchmark runs and human eval; Week 5: security review and private deploy validation (if selected); Week 6: final report + decision.

25:15 Marcus: benchmark details: we'll run three model variants - open quantized v1 (lower cost), standard baseline (better quality), and pinned dedicated instance. For each variant we'll report: p50/p90/p95 latencies, throughput (req/s), error rate, tokens in/out, estimated token cost, and quality pass rate.

28:40 Samir: for reporting format we prefer: 1) raw CSV per run (cols: timestamp, request_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, variant, error_flag, note), 2) summary spreadsheet with aggregated metrics per model/variant, 3) Redwood Console link with charts, and 4) a short runbook doc describing tuning steps applied.

31:05 Lena: agreed - and we'll also include a short executive one-pager with go/no-go recommendation (green/amber/red) and flagged remediation items.

34:50 Tom: network questions - if we go Private we need VPC peering or transit gateway and a diagram for our infra team. Also we need proof of key rotation policies.
34:58 Marcus: we'll provide network diagram, IP ranges, and KMS rotation details. For private on-prem there's extra lead time - estimate 2 weeks for infra work once contracts signed.

38:10 Samir: curious on warm cache behavior - if you run KV cache warm, what's the measurable improvement?
38:20 Marcus: typically p95 improves by 15-30% on repeated prefixes depending on model; we'll include a warm vs cold run comparison. We'll record both cold-start and warmed metrics.

41:12 Maya: acceptance criteria edge cases - model hallucination rate: how do we track?
41:20 Marcus: we'll add a hallucination tag in the human review sheet and include a summary: hallucination rate must be under 5% on sampled responses. If higher, that's a fail condition.

44:55 Lena: recap and go/no-go matrix we'll email: mandatory pass items: quality >=92% OR conditional remediation window, p95 thresholds (hosted/dedicated), availability 99.9%, token cost < $0.0006/token. Provide measurement method: 2k rep queries for baseline, 10k stress test; human eval 200 samples. Reports: raw CSV + aggregated sheet + console dashboard + one-pager.

48:10 Samir: ok we're aligned, just to confirm the human evaluation flow - Redwood provides anonymized output CSV, Aurelia does rating and shares results?
48:25 Marcus: yes either Aurelia rates and shares CSV back, or Redwood can coordinate the annotation; we'll leave that option open. We'll both sign off on the sample seed and rubric before the human eval run.

51:30 Tom: final security ask - share SOC2 and third-party pen test summary; Redwood to redact IPS if necessary.
51:40 Lena: noted, we'll attach those docs to the POC packet.

54:05 Lena: cool, thanks everyone. Next steps captured, we'll send POC doc and acceptance template by Wednesday, Samir to drop data samples by Friday, Marcus to schedule the first benchmark slot next week.

--- End transcript ---

Acceptance test (short form) to be attached as CSV template: columns = [test_id, prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_keywords, max_latency_ms, model_variant, observed_latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_usd, quality_pass_bool, hallucination_flag, notes].

Go/No-go thresholds (agreed):
- Quality: human pass rate >= 92% (85-92% conditional with 1-week remediation; <85% fail)
- Latency: hosted path p95 < 400ms; dedicated p95 < 300ms; p50 < 150ms expected
- Reliability: error rate <= 1% during benchmark runs
- Cost: average token cost across runs < $0.0006/token
- Hallucination: sampled hallucination rate < 5%

Reporting format (agreed):
- Raw CSV per run (see template columns)
- Aggregated spreadsheet with p50/p90/p95, throughput, cost, quality pass rate per model variant
- Redwood Console link for charts and traces (we will provide link and short guide)
- One-page executive summary with green/amber/red recommendation and remediation items
file_notes: POC scoping call focused on sign-off of acceptance tests and reporting format. Customer prefers human-eval driven quality gate and has strict cost and latency bounds. Action items and dates included.
